Definition: from G1537; the exterior; figuratively (as a preposition) aside from, besides:--but, except(-ed), other than, out of, outside, unless, without.
BiblicalUsage: ektós is a plain word for outside, except. In Matthew 23:26, the text says "that the outside of them may be clean also." In Acts 26:22, the text says "saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ektós shows us that God's Word means what it says, and this word is part of how He speaks plainly to us. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
